competition: Venezuela — Olimpiada Juvenil de Matemática (OJM), National Final (Prueba Final Nacional), top level (5th year of secondary school)

problems.problem: Let $P(n)$ and $S(n)$ denote, respectively, the product and the sum of the digits of the positive integer $n$. For example, $P(34)=12$ and $S(34)=7$. If $n$ is a two-digit number and $P(n)+S(n)=n$, what is the units digit of $n$?
We define a new operation on the set of real numbers by the formula $a*b=\dfrac{a+b}{2}$. If $x*(x*14)=x$, find the value of $x$.

A right triangle has legs of lengths $a$ and $b$. A circle of radius $r$ is tangent to both legs and has its centre on the hypotenuse of the right triangle. Prove that $$\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}=\frac{1}{r}.$$

A music band of the Venezuelan Association of Mathematical Competitions is marching in formation. At the start, the band forms a square with as many columns as rows, but later they change to the shape of a rectangle with five more columns than the number of rows. How many musicians does the band have?

On each planet of a solar system there is an astronomer observing the planet nearest to his own. The distances between the planets are pairwise distinct. Prove that if the number of planets is odd, then there is at least one planet that nobody observes.
Consider all the isosceles triangles whose vertices are vertices of a regular hexagon of area $1$. What is the average of the areas of these triangles?

Catia, Ana Laura, Magdalena, Gabriel, Víctor and Edgardo played darts in pairs (one woman and one man). Each of them scored, on each throw, as many points as the number of throws he or she made; that is, if someone made $10$ throws, he or she scored $10$ points per throw. Each of the women scored $45$ points more than her partner; moreover, we know that Catia made $7$ throws more than Edgardo and Víctor made $15$ throws more than Magdalena. Who was Catia's partner?

In the figure, $BCD$ is a quarter of a circle of radius $1$. The angle $BCA$ measures $60^\circ$ and $X$ is a point on the segment $CD$. If the area of the shaded region is half the area of the quarter circle $BCD$, what is the length of the segment $CX$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2005_p3_fig.png
Consider two positive three-digit numbers such that one of them has all its digits even and the other has all its digits odd. What is the smallest possible positive difference between the two?

An $m\times n$ rectangle ($m$ and $n$ natural numbers) is divided into unit squares. A ray of light enters the rectangle at one of its vertices, in the direction of the bisector of the right angle, and is reflected by the sides of the rectangle. How many squares does the ray of light pass through? (When the ray of light reaches a vertex of the rectangle again, it leaves.)
A number has $223$ digits and the product of its digits is $3^{446}$. What is the sum of its digits?
Find all solutions of the equation $m^2-3m+1=n^2+n-1$, where $m$ and $n$ are positive integers.

The sequence $a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4,\ldots$ is defined as follows: $$\begin{aligned} a_1&=a_2=1003,\\ a_3&=a_2-a_1=0,\\ a_4&=a_3-a_2=-1003,\end{aligned}$$ and so on; that is, $a_{n+1}=a_n-a_{n-1}$ for each $n\ge 2$. Compute the sum of the first $2006$ terms of the sequence.

José, Darío and Ana made a batch of labels. On each of them they wrote one of the numbers $2,3,4,5,6,7$ and $8$. Later Estrella joined the group and put a label on the forehead of each of her friends. José, Darío and Ana could not see the number on their own foreheads, but each of them could see the numbers of the other two friends. Estrella told them: “The numbers you have are not all different. Moreover, the product of the three numbers is a perfect square.” Could the three friends find out which number each of them had on his or her forehead? Explain your answer.
Consider an isosceles triangle $ABC$ with $\widehat{B}=\widehat{C}=\dfrac{2\pi}{5}$. Let $CD$ be the bisector of the angle $\widehat{ACB}$. Find the value of $\dfrac{BC}{AB-BC}$.

The shaded (black) polygon shown in the figure has been obtained from an equilateral triangle of side $12$ by removing the unshaded regions. Each of the sides of the shaded polygon is parallel to some side of the triangle. Three of the sides of the polygon measure $1$, $2$ and $3$, as shown. Compute the perimeter of the polygon, justifying your answer.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2007_p1_fig.png
It is known that a certain positive integer $n$ has $2$ positive divisors, while $n+1$ has $3$ positive divisors. How many positive divisors does $n+2$ have? Justify your answer.
Find all pairs of prime numbers $p$ and $q$ such that $p^2+q$ and $p^3+q^2$ are prime. Explain your answer.
Prove that $$\sqrt[3]{1-27\sqrt[3]{26}+9\sqrt[3]{26^2}}+\sqrt[3]{26}$$ is an integer, and compute it.
Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive integers such that $x+yz=82$ and $y+zx=62$. What values can the expression $z+xy$ take? Justify your answer.
Determine all prime numbers $p$ and $q$ such that $p$ divides $q+6$ and $q$ divides $p+7$.

A hexagon $ABCDEF$ has the following properties:

(a) The diagonals $AC$, $CE$ and $EA$ have the same length $\sqrt{85}$.

(b) The angles $ABC$ and $CDE$ are right angles.

(c) The lengths of the sides of the hexagon are six different integers.

Compute the smallest possible value of the perimeter of the hexagon.
For which values of $n$ is $2^8+2^{11}+2^n$ a perfect square?

The positive integers are placed as shown in the following array:

$$\begin{array}{r|cccccccccc} & \text{Col. 1} & & \text{Col. 2} & & \text{Col. 3} & & \text{Col. 4} & & \text{Col. 5} & \\ \hline\text{Row 1} & 1 & & 2 & & 5 & & 10 & & 17 & \cdots \\ & & & \downarrow & & \downarrow & & \downarrow & & \downarrow & \\\text{Row 2} & 4 & \leftarrow & 3 & & 6 & & 11 & & \vdots & \\ & & & & & \downarrow & & \downarrow & & & \\\text{Row 3} & 9 & \leftarrow & 8 & \leftarrow & 7 & & 12 & & & \\ & & & & & & & \downarrow & & & \\\text{Row 4} & 16 & \leftarrow & 15 & \leftarrow & 14 & \leftarrow & 13 & & & \\ & \vdots & & \vdots & & \vdots & & \vdots & & &\end{array}$$

(a) In which row and which column is the number $2008$?

(b) Give a formula for the integer located in row $m$ and column $n$ of the array above, in the case $m\le n$.

(c) Give a formula for the integer located in row $m$ and column $n$ of the array above, in the case $m>n$.
Find all quadruples of positive integers $(a,k,m,n)$ such that $a^k=a^m+a^n$.
A sequence of real numbers $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$ satisfies the relation $(n+2)a_{n+1}=na_n$ for every positive integer $n$. If $a_1=1005$, what is the value of $a_{2009}$?

Juana has a white $6\times 6$ board and wants to paint two of its squares black. Two colourings that differ by a rotation are considered equivalent; for example, the four colourings illustrated in the figure are all equivalent. In how many non-equivalent ways can Juana paint her board?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2009_1_p3_fig.png

$BD$ is a median of triangle $ABC$. The angle $ACB$ measures $30^\circ$ and the angle $ADB$ measures $45^\circ$. What is the measure of the angle $ABD$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2009_1_p4_fig.png
María writes three-digit natural numbers such that the middle digit is greater than the sum of the other two, for example $273$ and $494$. At most how many different numbers can María write?

With the four real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$, where $a<b<c<d$, one can form $6$ pairs. If each pair has a different sum and the four smallest sums are $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$, what are all the possible values of the number $d$?

The figure shows a rectangle $ABCD$ divided into three equal squares, and the angles $\alpha=\angle BAC$ and $\beta=\angle BAE$. Find the exact value, in degrees, of $\alpha+\beta$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2010_p3_fig.png

For a positive real number $x$, denote by $[x]$ the integer part of $x$ (the greatest integer not exceeding $x$) and by $\{x\}$ the fractional part of $x$, that is, $\{x\}=x-[x]$. For example, if $x=2.47$ then $[x]=2$ and $\{x\}=0.47$. Find all positive real numbers $x$ for which the sequence $\{x\},\ [x],\ x$ is a geometric progression.
Find all primes $p\ge 2$ such that $11p-8$ is a perfect cube.

In the figure, $ABCDE$ is a regular pentagon and $ABFGHIJKLM$ is a regular decagon.

(a) Prove that $D$ is the centre of the decagon.

(b) Find the measure of the angle $\angle DIG$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2011_1_p2_fig.png

Each positive integer $(1, 2, 3, \ldots)$ is painted yellow, blue or red, in such a way that there is at least one number of each colour. Is it possible to do this so that, for every pair of numbers of different colours, their sum has a colour different from the colours of both summands?

Each member of Luis's family drank coffee with milk at breakfast. They all drank the same amount, although the proportion of coffee and milk varied from cup to cup. If Luis drank one quarter of the total milk and one sixth of the total coffee,

(a) how many members are there in Luis's family?

(b) on average, what was the percentage of milk in the coffee with milk?
Find all integers $a$, different from $0$ and from $4$, such that the number $$\frac{a}{a-4}+\frac{2}{a}$$ is also an integer.

(a) Prove that for every $n$ $$n^2-(n+1)^2-(n+2)^2+(n+3)^2-(n+4)^2+(n+5)^2+(n+6)^2-(n+7)^2=0.$$

(b) The squares of the numbers from $1$ to $2012$ are written on the blackboard: $1^2, 2^2, 3^2, \ldots, 2012^2$. A sign $+$ or $-$ must be written in front of each number so that the algebraic sum of the $2012$ numbers is the smallest possible positive value. Determine this minimum and indicate a way of distributing the signs that achieves it.

Consider the points with both coordinates integers in the Cartesian plane. At the origin $(0,0)$ the number $1$ is placed, at $(1,0)$ the number $2$, at $(1,1)$ the number $3$, and so on: the positive integers are placed successively in a spiral around the origin (see the figure). Determine the coordinates of the point where $2012$ will be placed.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2012_1_p3_fig.png
Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle and $P$ an interior point such that $PA=5$, $PB=4$, $PC=3$. What is the measure of the angle $\angle BPC$?

The product of all the divisors of a natural number $n$ (including $1$ and $n$ itself) is equal to $n^4$.

(a) How many divisors does $n$ have?

(b) What is the smallest possible value of $n$?

Two circles are constructed as shown in the figure. The segment $AB$ is the diameter of the smaller circle. The centre $S$ of the larger circle lies on the smaller circle. The radius of the larger circle is $R$. Find the area of the shaded region in terms of $R$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2013_1_p2_fig.png
Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for all real $x$ and $y$ $$f(x)f(y)=f(x+y)+xy.$$

A flea is on the ground, at the foot of a staircase of $30$ steps. The flea can only jump $3$ steps up or $4$ steps down. In how many ways can it climb to step $22$ in the smallest possible number of jumps?

Consider the following two operations that can be applied to a fraction: (1) increase the numerator by $8$; (2) increase the denominator by $7$. Starting with the fraction $\frac{7}{8}$, after performing a total of $n$ operations of the types described, in some order, a fraction of equal value was obtained. What is the smallest possible value of $n$?

Let $f$ be a function from the positive reals to the positive reals such that $$f(x)f(y)-f(xy)=\frac{x}{y}+\frac{y}{x}$$ for all $x,y>0$.

(a) Find $f(1)$.

(b) Find an expression for $f(x)$.

The line $L$ passes through the vertex $A$ of a rectangle $ABCD$. The distance from the point $C$ to $L$ is $2$, and the distance from the point $D$ to $L$ is $6$. If $AD$ is twice $AB$, what is the length of $AD$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2014_1_p3_fig.png

Diego builds a sequence of integers in the following way: he starts by writing $2, 0, 1, 4$, and from then on he adds the last four numbers written and writes the units digit of that sum. Thus the first terms of the sequence are $2, 0, 1, 4, 7, 2, 4, \ldots$

(a) Will the initial numbers $2, 0, 1, 4$ appear again in this sequence, consecutively and in that order?

(b) Will the numbers $2, 0, 1, 5$ appear in this sequence, consecutively and in that order?
Find two perfect squares, each with $4$ digits, that differ by $2015$.

María wrote on the blackboard the numbers from $1$ to $2015$. Then she erased all the even numbers, and of those that remained she erased all the multiples of $3$.

(a) How many numbers remained on the blackboard?

(b) What is the sum of all of them?

Juan has three blank cards. On each of them he writes a different digit, from $0$ to $8$. Then he deals the cards to Ana, Berta and Claudia, giving one card to each. Each of them writes down the number on her card on a piece of paper. Then Juan collects the cards, shuffles them and deals them again. Each of the three girls writes down the number on her new card. This process is repeated a number of times. At the end, each girl adds up the numbers she wrote down. Ana's sum is $9$, Berta's is $25$ and Claudia's is $31$. What numbers were written on the cards? Find all the possibilities.

$ABC$ is a triangle with a right angle at $B$, with $AB=5$ cm and $BC=10$ cm. $\mathcal{C}$ is the circle with centre $A$ passing through $B$. $DEFG$ is a square contained in the triangle $ABC$, with the vertices $D$ and $E$ on the segment $BC$, the vertex $F$ on the segment $AC$ and the vertex $G$ on the circle $\mathcal{C}$. What is the area of $DEFG$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2015_1_p4_fig.png

Four girls attend a party, each accompanied by a brother. The girls are called Ana, Berta, Carmen and Dora. Their brothers are called, in some order, Juan, Luis, Mario and Pedro. From a tray with $38$ sweets, Ana took one, Berta two, Carmen three and Dora four. Juan took the same number of sweets as his sister, Luis took twice as many as his sister, Mario three times as many as his sister and Pedro four times as many as his sister. The tray was left empty. Determine the name of each girl's brother.

What is the smallest natural number that can be expressed as the sum of $9$ consecutive natural numbers and also as the sum of $10$ consecutive natural numbers?

Note: “natural” is the same as “positive integer”.
Find all real solutions $(x,y)$ of the system of equations $$x-\frac{1}{y}=\frac{8}{x},\qquad y-\frac{1}{x}=\frac{8}{y}.$$

Let $ABCD$ be a square, $E$ the midpoint of the side $CD$ and $M$ a point inside the square such that $\angle MAB=\angle MBC=\angle BME$. Find the measure of the angle $\angle MAB$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2016_1_p4_fig.png

Each of the $2017$ people who live on an island is either honest, and always tells the truth, or a liar, and always lies. More than a thousand islanders go to a banquet and sit around a round table. Each of them says: “Of the two people who are my neighbours, one is honest and the other is a liar”. What is the maximum number of honest people there can be on the island?

Ramón wrote a two-digit positive integer $n$. Then he swapped the positions of the digits of $n$ and obtained an integer $k$. Then he drew a right triangle with legs $(n+k)/2$ and $(n-k)/2$. If the hypotenuse of that triangle measures $\sqrt{2017}$, what are the values of $n$ and $k$?

$A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ and $E$ are collinear points such that $AB=BC=CD=DE=1$ cm. $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ are semicircles of radius $1$ cm with centres $B$ and $D$, respectively. $\mathcal{C}_3$ and $\mathcal{C}_4$ are circles of radius $4$ cm with centres $A$ and $E$, respectively, which meet at $F$. Determine the radius of the circle $\mathcal{C}_5$ that is externally tangent to $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ and internally tangent to $\mathcal{C}_3$ and $\mathcal{C}_4$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2017_1_p3_fig.png
Find all real solutions $(x,y)$ of the system of equations $$2^x+2^y=5\sqrt{2},\qquad 4^x+4^y=34.$$
Each side of a right triangle measures an integer number of centimetres. If one of the legs measures $17$ cm, what is the length of the hypotenuse?
How many ordered pairs $(a,b)$ of positive integers are there such that the least common multiple of $a$ and $b$ is $10800$?
Find all pairs of real numbers $(x,y)$ satisfying the system of equations $$\begin{aligned} 2x+3y&=10,\\ \frac{1}{x^2+1}+\frac{1}{y^2+1}&=\frac{4}{x^2+y^2+2}.\end{aligned}$$
What is the smallest possible value of $r$ such that an equilateral triangle of side $1$ can be completely covered by three identical discs of radius $r$?

Amanda wrote a $4$-digit positive integer $A$. Laura wrote a digit $x$ to the left of $A$ and a digit $y$ to the right of $A$, obtaining a $6$-digit integer $L$. Then Iván divided $L$ by $A$, obtaining $21$ as quotient and $0$ as remainder. Determine the values of $A$ and $L$.
Find all real solutions of the system $$\begin{aligned} 4^x+y&=4030,\\ 17\cdot 2^x+2y&=2019.\end{aligned}$$

Lisandro had a pile of $2019$ stones. He divided the pile into two non-empty piles, multiplied the numbers of stones in the two piles and wrote the result on the blackboard. Then he chose a pile with more than one stone and performed the same operation. He continued in this way until every pile had only one stone. At that moment he added all the numbers written on the blackboard. Is it possible to determine the result obtained? If it is possible, find it.

Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle. Let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of $AB$ and $BC$, respectively. Let $P$ be a point outside $ABC$ such that $APC$ is isosceles and right-angled at $P$. The lines $PM$ and $AN$ meet at $I$. Prove that $CI$ is the bisector of the angle $\angle ACM$.
For which positive integers $n$ is the number $3^n+4n-1$ a perfect square?
Using only the digits $1$, $2$ and $3$, how many fifteen-digit numbers can be formed such that any two neighbouring digits differ by $1$? (An example of such a number is $212123232123212$.)
Let $p(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients. If $p(1)$ and $p(0)$ are odd, prove that $p(x)=0$ has no integer solutions.

$ABCD$ is a rectangle. The red circle is tangent to the sides $DA$, $AB$ and $BC$. The yellow circle is tangent to the red circle and to the sides $BC$ and $CD$. The common tangent of the two circles at their point of contact passes through $D$. If the area of the yellow circle is $1\ \text{cm}^2$, what is the area of the red circle?

A box contains $19$ coloured balls. If any six balls are drawn, at least two and at most four of them are of the same colour. It is known that at least one of the balls is blue, and that there are more red balls than blue ones. Determine, if possible, the exact number of blue balls and of red balls in the box.
Find all solutions of the system of equations $$\begin{aligned} abc&=240,\\ ac+b&=46,\\ a+bc&=64.\end{aligned}$$

Find the smallest positive integer $n$ satisfying the following two conditions:

1. The sum of the digits of $n$ is $50$.

2. The sum of the digits of $2n$ (twice $n$) is $64$.

$ABC$ is a triangle with a right angle at $B$, with $AB=3$ cm and $BC=4$ cm. $\Omega$ is the circle inscribed in $ABC$, tangent to the sides $AB$, $BC$ and $CA$. $\omega$ is the circle tangent to $\Omega$ and to the sides $BC$ and $AC$ of the triangle $ABC$. Find the radii of $\Omega$ and of $\omega$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2021_p4_fig.png
Let $u$, $v$ and $w$ be real numbers such that $$3^u=5,\qquad 4^v=9,\qquad 5^w=32.$$ Determine the value of the product $uvw$.

The number $2$ is written on a blackboard. Ana and Beto play alternately, starting with Ana, replacing the number on the blackboard by a larger number that does not exceed three times that number. For example, at the start of the game Ana can replace the $2$ by $3$, $4$, $5$ or $6$. Then Beto must write a number larger than the one Ana wrote but not exceeding its triple, and so on. The first player to write a number greater than or equal to $2022$ loses (and the other player wins). Determine whether one of the players has a winning strategy, and describe it.

Note: A winning strategy is a method of play that guarantees victory to the player who uses it, regardless of what the other player does.

Two circles of radii $3$ and $6$ are externally tangent, and both are internally tangent to another circle of radius $9$. A chord of the circle of radius $9$ is tangent, at two different points, to the other two circles. What is the length of that chord?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2022_p3_fig.png

Ten people attend a meeting. It is known that in every possible group of three of them there are at least two who do not know each other. Prove that there are at least four people who do not know one another.
Find all real solutions of the equation $$2^x=\sqrt{9\cdot 2^{x+2}-128}.$$
Find the smallest positive integer $n$ such that the sum of the digits of $n$ and the sum of the digits of $n+1$ are both multiples of $13$.

$ABCD$ is a square of side $2$ cm. $\omega_1$ is a semicircle with diameter $AB$. $\omega_2$ is a circle tangent to $\omega_1$ and to the sides $BC$ and $CD$ of the square. Find the radius of $\omega_2$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ve_2023_p3_fig.png
Let $f$ be a function such that, whenever $a$, $b$ and $n$ are positive integers with $a+b=2^n$, we have $f(a)+f(b)=n^2$. Find the value of $f(2023)$.
Find a positive integer $n$ and a prime number $p$ such that $1+211p=n^3$.

If $a$ and $b$ are two positive integers, we say that $f(a,b)=1$ if $ab+1$ is a perfect square. For example, $f(3,8)=1$ because $3\cdot 8+1=25=5^2$. If $ab+1$ is not a perfect square but there exists a positive integer $r$ such that $f(a,r)=1$ and $f(r,b)=1$, then we say that $f(a,b)=2$. If $f(a,b)$ is neither $1$ nor $2$, but there exist positive integers $r$ and $s$ such that $f(a,r)=f(r,s)=f(s,b)=1$, we say that $f(a,b)=3$, and so on.

a) Prove that $f(n,n+2)=1$ for every positive integer $n$.

b) What is $f(1,2)$?

c) What is $f(1,4)$?

Eight chess players play in a tournament in which each pair of them must play each other once and only once. At a certain moment it is observed that if any five players are taken (out of the eight), then there are at least two of them who have not yet played each other. What is the maximum number of games that can have been played up to that moment?

Two circles of equal radius are inscribed in a rectangle whose sides measure $64$ cm and $50$ cm. The circles are tangent to each other, and each of them is tangent to two sides of the rectangle, as shown in the figure. What is the radius of the circles?
